name: Fano insurgency in Amhara
started: 2023-08-01 (approximate; Fano has fought the federal government since 2023)
summary: Fano, a loose network of Amhara militias that fought alongside the government in the 2020 to 2022 Tigray war, has been in revolt since 2023. In 2026 it disrupted the national election, joined a coalition with the TPLF and OLA, and attacked federal supply lines as the army fought in Tigray.

sides.name: Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM) and other Fano groups
members: Regional Fano commands in Gojjam, Gondar, Wollo and Shewa
backers: Eritrea (existing ties with Amhara rebels, per CTP)

background: Fano turned on the federal government after being sidelined in the Pretoria peace process and over disputed land in western and southern Tigray that Amhara nationalists claim. Its fighters control or contest much of the Amhara countryside and repeatedly cut the main roads linking Addis Ababa to the north.

Its alliance with the TPLF, its former enemy, is pragmatic and fragile because the two still dispute the same land. That matters because any Fano advance on the A2 and B30 highways threatens the army's supply lines into Tigray.
year: A late-2025 Fano offensive took towns around Lalibela and along the A2 and B22 roads before ENDF drone counterattacks cleared them. In February 2026 Fano seized key towns and roads as army units were redeployed toward Tigray. On election day, 1 June 2026, the AFNM launched 'Operation Ayisha Seid', with ACLED recording at least 90 clashes, the most on any single day since 2023, after 108 clashes in all of May. In mid-August leader Zemene Kassie confirmed a coalition with the TPLF and OLA. During the September to October Tigray fighting, the AFNM pushed down the A2 with the TDF, captured Wurgessa (3 Oct) and Mehal Meda (7 Oct), attacked Dabat north of Gondar and fought around Lalibela and Mekane Selam.
situation: As of October 2026 Fano is active across North Wollo, North Shewa, Gondar and Gojjam, cutting the A2, B21 and B30 roads and holding some towns, while federal forces are concentrated in Tigray.
technical: ACLED recorded 108 Fano clashes in May 2026 and at least 90 on 1 June 2026, the busiest day of the insurgency.
Federal counterinsurgency relies on drone strikes; CTP notes ENDF drone counterattacks cleared Fano gains around Lalibela in late 2025.
Key roads contested: A2 (Addis Ababa to Dessie, Woldia and Mekelle), B21 (via Mekane Selam), B30 (Gondar to Shire), B22 (Lalibela area).
October 2026 captures claimed or reported: Wurgessa on the A2 (about 30 miles south of Woldia) and Mehal Meda (about 50 miles north of Debre Berhan).
Fano and OLA factions clashed in Oromia in early August 2026, and ACLED reported some OLA factions working with the government against Fano, underlining the alliance's limits.
After 3 Oct 2026 the AFNM attacked ENDF positions around Mekane Selam, about 110 miles west of Dessie, cutting the B21 highway; control of the town was contested.
Precedent: a mid-2024 Fano offensive briefly took B30 towns north of Gondar and entered part of Gondar city (CTP).
Fano attacks around Lalibela in late September and early October 2026 kept Lalibela airport closed to flights (CTP, 29 Sep 2026).

Alliance politics: Fano opposes ethnic federalism while the OLA supports it, and Fano claims land in western and southern Tigray, so CTP expects these disputes to block a coherent coalition with the TPLF.
casualties: No fatality total was found for October 2025 to October 2026. Event counts from ACLED (over 100 clashes a month in mid-2026) suggest well over 1,000 deaths a year, so the 'high' label is an estimate.
displaced: Included in Ethiopia's national IDP figure of 1,919,993 (UNHCR, 31 Aug 2026); no Amhara-specific figure found.

timeline.event: AFNM launches Operation Ayisha Seid on election day; at least 90 clashes recorded.
Zemene Kassie confirms a coalition with the TPLF and OLA (mid-August).
AFNM captures Wurgessa on the A2.
AFNM captures Mehal Meda and attacks Dabat.

outlook: Watch whether Fano exploits the army's focus on Tigray to take and hold district towns or cut the A2 for longer, and whether land disputes with the TPLF break the alliance.

zones.name: North Wollo and the A2 corridor
zones.note: Woldia, Kobo, Lalibela and Wurgessa; Fano attacks on army supply lines to Tigray.

zones.name: North Shewa (Mehal Meda)
zones.note: AFNM captured Mehal Meda on 7 Oct 2026.

zones.name: Gondar and the B30
zones.note: Fano attacks on Dabat and the road north to Tigray.

battles.name: Fano captures of Wurgessa and Mehal Meda
battles.place: Mehal Meda, North Shewa, Amhara, Ethiopia
battles.outcome: AFNM took Wurgessa on the A2 (3 Oct) and Mehal Meda (7 Oct), attacked Dabat and contested Mekane Selam.
battles.forces: AFNM fighters against ENDF garrisons stretched by the Tigray campaign.
battles.significance: Threatens the army's main supply road to Tigray.

battles.name: Operation Ayisha Seid (election-day offensive)
battles.outcome: At least 90 clashes across Amhara on election day, the most on any day since 2023.
battles.forces: AFNM units region-wide; government vehicle ban.
battles.losses: No fatality figure in ACLED's comment.
battles.significance: Showed Fano's ability to coordinate region-wide and disrupt the national election.
